comments.title: Use the repository test filename convention
comments.body:
**Use the repository test filename convention**

The unit test is named `discount.spec.js`, not the required `discount.test.js`; the CI `node --test` discovery pattern will not select this filename. Rename it to `discount.test.js` so the test is discovered.

<details><summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

kind: standard, confidence: high, rule: .github/copilot-instructions.md:4
</details>

| R2 | PR body: The SAVE10 coupon takes 10% off the subtotal. | O2 | 0/1 obligations covered (not fully covered). Requires an assertion of the discounted subtotal, not merely a truthy result. |
| R3 | PR body: A total of 100 or more gets 5 off. | O3 | 0/1 obligations covered (not fully covered). Requires assertions at the 100 threshold and below it. |
| R4 | PR body: Store credit is subtracted from the total, which never goes below zero. | O4, O5 | 0/2 obligations covered (not fully covered). Split into separate obligations for subtracting credit and flooring the resulting total at zero. |

**Test layers: checked.** Inspected the Node 22 CI configuration and JavaScript tests across src, eval, and eval-sandbox. The changed test calls the exported function directly with node:test and node:assert, so the tested seam is unit-level; no component, integration, or end-to-end assertions cover this function. No higher-layer-only logic is a pushdown candidate. This was a static review; tests were not executed.
